pageCache.pageTitle: Claires Court School | Independent All-Through Boys & Girls School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Claires Court
Early Years / Nursery
Claires Court Nursery in Maidenhead provides educational childcare that gives children the space to enjoy their early years while offering a nurturing, purposeful and ambitious start to learning.
Juniors
Claires Court Juniors in Maidenhead gives pupils the space to enjoy childhood while providing a broad, nurturing and ambitious education that builds confidence, curiosity and strong foundations for the future.
Seniors
Claires Court Seniors in Maidenhead offers an ambitious independent education for pupils aged 11 to 16. Small classes ensure pupils are known, stretched and supported, with focused teaching, individual attention and a wide range of opportunities that build confidence, develop strengths and prepare them for GCSEs and beyond.
Sixth Form
Claires Court Sixth Form in Maidenhead offers an ambitious independent education for students aged 16 to 18. Small classes mean students are known, stretched and supported, with focused teaching, strong relationships and a broad choice of academic and vocational pathways to prepare them for university, apprenticeships and beyond.
Pathways
Claires Court Sixth Form offers high performance pathways for students with the ambition and potential to excel. Through expert teaching, individual support and specialist opportunities, students are stretched to achieve at the highest level while developing the confidence, discipline and independence needed for their next step.
History and Stability
Claires Court has been part of the Maidenhead community since 1960.
Today, that established heritage is strengthened by being part of LTC Education Group, backed by the Licensed Trade Charity, an organisation with more than 200 years of history and long term financial strength.
For parents, this combination of experience, stability and responsible investment provides confidence that Claires Court is a secure choice for their child’s education, now and for the future.
School Admissions & Fees
We can help every step of the way. Our School Admissions team is available to answer any queries you may have about boarding school admissions, please don’t hesitate to contact us at registrar@clairescourt.com
Associations

Parent Partnership
Working together to help every child thrive
At Claires Court, we believe the strongest foundations for learning are built when school and home work together. From your child’s very first visit, we take the time to get to know your family, recognising that parents and guardians know their child best.
By working in partnership, we create a consistent and supportive approach that helps every pupil feel happy, secure and confident as they begin their educational journey. Open communication, mutual trust and shared understanding enable us to provide the very best experience for every child.
Helping Children Feel Safe and Secure
Starting Nursery or Reception is an exciting milestone, and we understand that a positive start makes all the difference.
To help every child settle happily into their new environment, all new pupils receive a home visit from a member of our Early Years team before they join us. This is an invaluable opportunity to begin building relationships with your child and family, while helping us understand their interests, routines and individual needs.
We also offer settling in sessions before your child’s first day, allowing them to become familiar with their new surroundings, meet their teachers and begin making new friends at their own pace. These early experiences help children feel confident, safe and ready to embrace their new adventure.
An Ongoing Partnership
From the moment your child joins Claires Court, they will be supported by a dedicated Key Person who plays an important role in their Early Years experience.
Your child’s Key Person will build a close relationship with them, monitor their learning and development, celebrate their achievements and provide regular updates on their progress. They are also your first point of contact, ensuring that communication between home and school is open, supportive and meaningful.
We understand that starting Nursery is a significant milestone for parents as well as children. Our experienced Early Years team is always on hand to answer questions, offer reassurance and provide guidance throughout your child’s journey.
Supporting Children and Parents
We know that children flourish when school and home work together.
We value regular conversations with parents and guardians, whether it’s a quick update at the end of the day or a more detailed discussion about your child’s progress. If you would like to talk to us in more depth, we are always happy to arrange a phone call or one to one meeting at a convenient time.
By sharing observations, celebrating achievements and discussing any questions together, we can ensure every pupil receives the support they need to develop with confidence, both in school and at home.

pageCache.pageTitle: Moving to Senior School | Claires Court Juniors
pageCache.text:
Moving to Senior School
Preparing for What's Next
Transition begins long before pupils reach Year 6.
Throughout the Junior School, we nurture the independence, resilience and study skills that help children flourish in Senior School. As pupils grow in confidence, they are encouraged to take greater responsibility for their learning, preparing them not only for Year 7 but for the opportunities and challenges that lie beyond.
Because we know every child as an individual, we can ensure each pupil moves on at the right pace, with the right level of challenge and support.
Getting to Know Our Senior Schools
We believe that familiarity builds confidence.
To help pupils and families understand what lies ahead, we introduce our Senior Schools gradually through a programme of events and experiences.
Year 4
Families are invited to a dedicated Senior School event, including presentations from the Heads of Senior Boys and Senior Girls, providing an early insight into the next stage of the Claires Court journey.
Year 5
Every pupil enjoys a Senior School Taster Day, experiencing lessons, meeting teachers and discovering what life is like in either our Senior Boys or Senior Girls School. It’s an exciting opportunity to explore new subjects, experience specialist facilities and begin looking ahead with confidence.
A Smooth Transition in Year 6
As pupils prepare for Year 7, our Junior and Senior teams work together to make the move as seamless as possible.
Throughout Year 6, pupils spend time with Senior School staff through lessons and extended activities, allowing teachers to get to know them before they begin their next chapter.
Behind the scenes, our teachers provide a thorough handover, sharing each pupil’s academic progress, strengths and pastoral needs. This ensures every child arrives in Year 7 feeling known, understood and ready to thrive from day one.
Supporting Every Family
Every family’s journey is unique, and we’re here to support you throughout the decision-making process.
As an all-through school, we expect most of our pupils to continue into our Senior Schools, benefiting from the continuity of education and the strong relationships they’ve already built. However, we recognise that every family will make the decision that is right for their child.
Individual meetings are held with Mrs Kirby during Years 5 and 6, giving parents and guardians the opportunity to discuss their child’s progress, aspirations and next steps in a relaxed and supportive setting.
Continue the Journey with Claires Court
The transition to Senior School is an exciting new beginning, and we’d be delighted to show you what comes next.
Visit our Senior Schools, meet our dedicated staff and discover how we help every pupil move forward with confidence, purpose and ambition.

Our Tailored Curriculum
Designed around every pupil, shaped for future success
At Claires Court, we know that no two children learn in the same way. That’s why our curriculum is carefully tailored to challenge, support and inspire every pupil, helping them develop the knowledge, skills and confidence to achieve their full potential.
Purposefully small class sizes, together with our experienced teachers and teaching assistants, allow us to personalise learning for every child. Through regular assessment and a deep understanding of each pupil’s progress, we provide the right level of challenge while making learning engaging, enjoyable and meaningful.
Our Teaching Model
Our teaching model combines the expertise of experienced Junior School teachers with specialist subject teachers, ensuring pupils benefit from both continuity in their learning and expert subject knowledge.
Every pupil receives specialist teaching in:
From Year 3, pupils also benefit from specialist Art and Computing lessons. In Years 5 and 6, Drama is taught by specialist teachers, providing greater depth, challenge and preparation for Senior School.
Physical Education
Swimming
Music
Modern Foreign Languages
High Expectations for Every Learner
We believe every pupil should be challenged to achieve their very best.
Our teachers know every child’s strengths, interests and next steps, enabling them to adapt lessons to suit individual learning needs. Whether pupils need additional support or greater stretch, learning is carefully differentiated so everyone can make excellent progress.
By mastering fundamental skills before moving on to new concepts, pupils develop secure foundations and the confidence to tackle increasingly complex learning. Our teachers encourage pupils to think independently, ask questions and embrace challenges with curiosity and resilience.
As a partner school with Buckinghamshire Council for the 11+, we are also able to support families as they begin considering future Senior School pathways.
Developing Independent Learners
Learning is about much more than acquiring knowledge.
Our curriculum encourages pupils to become independent thinkers, confident communicators and collaborative learners. Through carefully planned enquiry based learning, pupils explore topics by investigating thought provoking questions, researching information and developing their own ideas and solutions.
This approach nurtures curiosity, creativity and problem solving while helping children develop the confidence to think for themselves and work effectively with others. Assessment and feedback are carefully tailored to support every pupil’s progress and encourage continuous improvement.
The Claires Court Essentials
The Claires Court Essentials sit at the heart of our learning philosophy and underpin every aspect of school life.
From Nursery onwards, pupils are encouraged to develop the skills, behaviours and attitudes they need to flourish both in school and beyond. We believe that making mistakes is an important part of learning, helping children build resilience, confidence and a positive approach to new challenges.
Our curriculum encourages pupils to become:
These qualities prepare pupils not only for academic success, but for life beyond the classroom.
Critical thinkers
Risk takers
Reflective learners
Effective communicators
Problem solvers
Inquirers
Collaborative learners
Creative thinkers
Learning Development
Every child deserves the opportunity to succeed.
Our Learning Development Department supports pupils who may need additional help with reading, spelling or numeracy. Children are assessed when they join Claires Court and, if additional needs are identified either at admission or during their time with us, our Head of Learning Development works closely with teachers and parents and guardians to develop appropriate support strategies.
Support is always tailored to individual needs, ensuring every pupil is given the opportunity to thrive academically while building confidence in their own abilities. Where specialist support is recommended, families are fully involved in discussing the most appropriate next steps.
A strong sense of a proud community allows the pupils to feel secure.
Creative Arts
Creativity is an essential part of a well rounded education.
Performing Arts play an important role in Junior School life, giving pupils opportunities to express themselves, build confidence and develop new talents. Whether performing on stage, creating artwork or learning a musical instrument, pupils are encouraged to explore their creativity and celebrate their achievements.
These experiences complement academic learning and help children develop confidence, collaboration and self expression that will benefit them throughout their education.
Discover Our Tailored Curriculum
Every child deserves an education that recognises their individuality, nurtures their strengths and inspires them to aim high.
Visit Claires Court to see our tailored curriculum in action, meet our dedicated teaching team and discover how we help every pupil achieve, belong and thrive.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Arts | Senior Boys | Claires Court
pageCache.text:
The Arts
Creativity in every pupil
The Arts play an important role in life at Claires Court. Through drama, music and art, boys are encouraged to explore new ideas, express themselves with confidence and develop skills that extend far beyond the classroom.
Whether performing on stage, creating original artwork or discovering a love of music, every pupil is challenged to experiment, collaborate and grow creatively. These experiences nurture confidence, resilience and individuality while enriching every aspect of school life.
Drama
Drama is for everyone at Senior Boys.
For some pupils, that means performing in front of an audience. For others, it is discovering their strengths behind the scenes through lighting, sound, stage management or set design. Whatever their interests, boys develop valuable communication, teamwork and creative thinking skills.
Drama is taught as part of the curriculum and is also a popular co curricular activity. In Years 7 and 8, pupils showcase their growing confidence and performance skills through the annual Drama Festivals, while regular theatre visits to local venues and London’s West End broaden their cultural experiences and inspire future performances.
Music
Music is a vibrant part of everyday life at Claires Court, with opportunities for boys of every ability to perform, create and develop their musical talents.
Whether taking their first instrumental lessons or performing as experienced musicians, pupils are encouraged to explore a wide range of musical styles and discover music that inspires them.
A varied programme of ensembles and clubs includes:
Throughout the year, boys perform in informal concerts, formal performances and school events, sharing their progress with families and the wider school community.
Instrumental tuition is delivered by an experienced team of specialist visiting music teachers, ensuring pupils receive expert guidance while developing their confidence and musicianship.
Claires Court Choristers
Senior Boys’ Voices
Guitar Ensemble
Mixed Instrumental Ensemble
IT in Music
Art
Art encourages boys to think independently, take creative risks and develop their own artistic style.
Working with a wide range of materials and techniques, pupils learn how different media can be used to communicate ideas while making confident creative decisions of their own. The result is imaginative, original work that is proudly displayed throughout the school.
The department’s commitment to creativity is reflected in the success of our pupils, who regularly receive recognition at the ISA Regional Art and Craft Competition. These achievements celebrate not only artistic talent but also the curiosity, perseverance and individuality that underpin every project.
Opportunities beyond the curriculum
Creativity does not stop when lessons finish.
A wide range of performances, ensembles, productions, exhibitions and clubs gives boys the opportunity to develop their interests further, collaborate with others and share their talents with the wider school community.
These experiences help pupils build confidence, communicate effectively and discover passions that often remain with them long after they leave Claires Court.
Visit our Senior Boys School
The best way to experience the creative opportunities at Claires Court is to see them for yourself.
Visit our Senior Boys School to explore our facilities, meet our specialist teachers and discover how drama, music and art help every boy develop confidence, creativity and a lifelong appreciation of the arts.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Arts | Senior Girls | Claires Court
pageCache.text:
The Arts
Creativity in every pupil
The arts play a vital role in life at Claires Court. Through art, drama and music, every girl is encouraged to explore her creativity, express herself with confidence and develop skills that will benefit her throughout school and beyond.
Whether performing on stage, creating original artwork, composing music or working behind the scenes, pupils are supported to discover their talents in an environment where creativity is celebrated and individuality is valued.
Drama
Drama at Claires Court is about much more than performance. It develops communication, collaboration, resilience and self-confidence, giving pupils the opportunity to express themselves while learning skills that will support them throughout their lives.
Drama is taught as part of the curriculum and is also a vibrant part of our co-curricular programme. Throughout the year, pupils perform in a variety of productions, from large-scale musicals to smaller showcases, with opportunities both on stage and behind the scenes in lighting, sound, costume, hair and make-up.
Recent productions have included Oh Britannia, celebrating British culture, and the original musical Living the Dream. Building on their success, pupils continue to collaborate on original productions, bringing together creativity, performance and teamwork from across the Senior School.
Year 7 and Year 8 pupils also take part in an annual Performing Arts Evening, celebrating creativity, teamwork and performance.
For GCSE Drama students, regular visits to local and West End theatres enrich classroom learning and broaden their cultural experience. Pupils can also choose to study LAMDA through our after-school programme, with higher grades offering the opportunity to gain valuable UCAS tariff points.
Art
Art and Design encourages pupils to think independently, experiment with ideas and develop their own creative voice.
Many girls choose Art at GCSE, exploring a wide range of disciplines including:
Alongside practical work, pupils study artists from different periods and cultures, developing the ability to analyse artwork and communicate their own creative intentions with confidence.
Weekly Art and Textiles clubs, together with daily GCSE support sessions, provide additional opportunities to work on larger projects, many of which are displayed throughout the school. Visits to galleries and museums further inspire pupils and support their creative development.
Our specialist facilities include dedicated Art and Textiles studios alongside a purpose-built observational drawing room equipped with standing easels.
Claires Court is proud to host the Regional ISA Art Competition each year and our pupils are regular award winners. Annual exhibitions celebrate the exceptional creativity and achievements of our young artists.

Music
Music is at the heart of school life, providing opportunities for every girl to perform, compose, collaborate and develop as a musician.
Our curriculum combines listening, performing, composing and music technology, introducing pupils to a wide range of musical styles while encouraging creativity, discussion and independent thinking.
Girls can take part in an extensive range of musical activities, including:
Regular concerts, productions, showcases, inter-house competitions and community performances give pupils numerous opportunities to perform, often alongside Senior Boys and Sixth Form students.
Our Music Department benefits from excellent facilities, including dedicated teaching rooms, three practice rooms and a professional music studio equipped with Mac computers, Logic Pro X, Sibelius and industry-standard recording technology. These resources enable pupils to develop both their musical and digital skills in a professional environment.

Opportunities to perform and create
The arts are woven throughout school life.
Whether taking part in a concert, exhibiting artwork, performing in a musical or contributing behind the scenes, every girl is encouraged to participate, challenge herself and celebrate her achievements.
These experiences nurture creativity, collaboration, communication and confidence. These qualities support success not only in school, but throughout higher education, future careers and everyday life.

The best way to experience the creativity and energy of our Arts programme is to visit us.
Meet our specialist teachers, explore our creative spaces and discover how every girl is encouraged to develop her talents, express her individuality and build confidence through the arts.

pageCache.pageTitle: Academic Approach | Senior Boys | Claires Court
pageCache.text:
Academic Approach
High Expectations, Personalised Support
At Claires Court, we believe academic success is about more than examination results. It is about helping every boy develop the confidence, knowledge and learning habits to achieve his personal best.
Our broad and varied curriculum is designed to stimulate curiosity, encourage independent thinking and challenge every pupil to reach his potential. Through expert teaching, high expectations and personalised support, boys develop the skills they need to succeed at GCSE, Sixth Form and beyond.
A curriculum designed for success
Every lesson is planned to engage, challenge and support pupils throughout their Senior School journey.
Our curriculum combines academic rigour with opportunities for creativity, collaboration and critical thinking, ensuring boys gain the knowledge and confidence to thrive in every subject.
Central to our approach are the Claires Court Essentials, which encourage pupils to become resilient, resourceful and reflective learners. Rather than simply recalling facts, boys are encouraged to question, investigate and apply their learning to solve problems and make meaningful connections across subjects.
Learning with purpose
We believe boys learn best when they are actively involved in the learning process.
Across many subjects, lessons are built around carefully constructed questions and real world challenges. This problem solving approach encourages pupils to investigate ideas, evaluate information and develop their own understanding rather than simply memorising facts.
Our focus is on developing secure understanding through mastery. By deepening knowledge before moving on, boys become confident learners who are well prepared for the demands of GCSE study and future learning.
Measuring progress, supporting achievement
Regular feedback helps every pupil understand how they are progressing and where they can improve.
Throughout the year, boys complete Common Tasks, with every pupil in the year group sitting the same assessment in each subject once per term. These assessments provide valuable feedback for pupils, parents and teachers while helping to celebrate achievement and identify opportunities for further development.
Parents and guardians receive regular grade cards throughout the academic year, together with detailed subject reports that provide a clear picture of progress and next steps. Our one hour lessons also maximise learning, concentration and collaboration throughout the school day.
Across the school, the academic curriculum provides a broad and coherent education for pupils of all ages, and fully supports the learning principles and philosophy of the School, and the high level of pupils’ achievements.
– ISI Inspection Report

As pupils move into Key Stage 4, they receive expert guidance to help them choose GCSE subjects that reflect their interests, strengths and future aspirations.

Our ambition is for every boy to leave Claires Court with results that reflect his ability, together with the confidence, resilience and learning skills to flourish in Sixth Form and beyond.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pastoral Care | Senior Boys | Claires Court
pageCache.text:
Senior Boys Pastoral Care
Every boy known and supported
At Claires Court, outstanding pastoral care is at the heart of everything we do. We believe boys achieve their best when they feel known, valued and supported, both in and beyond the classroom.
From the moment your son joins us, he becomes part of a close-knit community where trusted relationships, high expectations and genuine care help him grow in confidence. Our pastoral approach is closely connected to academic life, wellbeing and personal development, ensuring every pupil has the support they need to thrive.
Support that starts with strong relationships
Every boy has a Form Teacher who is his first point of contact for guidance and support.
Seeing pupils every day, Form Teachers build strong relationships and get to know each individual, helping them navigate school life while supporting their personal, social, health, citizenship and careers education.
This close partnership between pupils, teachers and families creates a culture of trust, openness and approachability, ensuring every boy feels listened to, encouraged and understood.
A culture of care and respect
Pastoral care is not something that happens in isolation. It underpins every aspect of school life.
We know that pupils flourish academically, socially and emotionally when they know they are supported. By creating an environment built on kindness, mutual respect and high expectations, we help boys develop resilience, confidence and the character to overcome challenges.
Every member of staff plays a role in creating a community where pupils feel safe to ask questions, seek support and become the very best version of themselves.
Celebrating character
Our Claires Court Key Value Award celebrates the qualities that help pupils become positive members of the school community.
Through their everyday actions, boys demonstrate responsibility, respect, kindness and a commitment to others. Their achievements are recognised by both staff and peers, with Key Value badges awarded as pupils progress through the school.
Awards are typically achieved as follows:
The programme reinforces our belief that character is just as important as academic success and encourages pupils to make a positive contribution to school life every day.
Bronze, end of Year 7
Silver, Year 8 or Year 9
Gold, Year 10 or Year 11
Platinum, Year 12 or Year 13
Working with Boys
Our Working with Boys programme helps pupils develop the confidence, understanding and values they need to thrive in today’s world.
Built around the principles of gentle masculinity and mutual respect, the programme encourages boys to treat everyone with dignity, empathy and consideration. Pupils explore topics such as positive relationships, respect for others and the importance of challenging harmful attitudes, helping them become thoughtful, responsible young men.
These conversations form an important part of preparing pupils for life beyond school and the wider communities they will be part of.
Specialist wellbeing support
Supporting wellbeing means caring for the whole child.
Our on-site School Nurses are available throughout the school day, providing support for physical health, emotional wellbeing and mental health. Working alongside our safeguarding and pastoral teams, they help ensure that no pupil feels overlooked or unsupported.
Based within dedicated wellbeing centres, the nursing team can also access specialist counselling and psychological services when additional support is needed, giving families confidence that expert help is always close at hand.
Discover the Claires Court difference
The best way to experience the supportive atmosphere at Claires Court is to visit us.
Meet our staff, talk to our pupils and discover how our pastoral care helps every boy feel valued, supported and ready to achieve his full potential.

Senior Boys Sports
A lifelong love of sport
Sport is an integral part of life at Claires Court. Every boy is encouraged to take part, develop new skills and enjoy being active, whether he is discovering a new sport or competing at the highest level.
With an extensive fixture programme, A and B teams across most age groups and a wide variety of sporting opportunities, every pupil has the chance to represent the school, challenge themselves and experience the benefits of teamwork, resilience and healthy competition.
Sport for every pupil
Our philosophy is simple. We want every boy to enjoy sport and leave school with the confidence and motivation to lead an active, healthy lifestyle.
Our experienced PE teachers and specialist coaches create an environment where pupils are supported to develop their skills, improve their performance and enjoy being part of a team. Boys are encouraged to challenge themselves, celebrate success and learn from setbacks, building resilience alongside sporting ability.
Many members of our sports staff coach at international level and continue to compete in their own sports, bringing a wealth of expertise and enthusiasm to every lesson and training session.

Our location provides access to sporting opportunities that few schools can match.

Senior boys can choose to sail, paddle or row throughout the year, developing technical skills while enjoying the physical and mental benefits of outdoor activity. Every pupil is encouraged to explore different sports, develop new skills and represent the school with pride.

pageCache.pageTitle: Academic Approach | Senior Girls | Claires Court
pageCache.text:
Academic Approach
High Expectations, Personalised Support
At Claires Court, academic success is about more than examination results. It’s about helping every girl develop the confidence, knowledge and learning habits to achieve her personal best and embrace the opportunities ahead.
Our broad and balanced curriculum is designed to stimulate curiosity, encourage independent thinking and challenge every pupil to reach her potential. Through expert teaching, high expectations and personalised support, we create an environment where girls are inspired to ask questions, solve problems and develop a lifelong love of learning.
A Curriculum Designed for Success
Every lesson is carefully planned to engage, stretch and support learners at every stage of their education.
Our curriculum combines academic rigour with opportunities for creativity, collaboration and critical thinking, ensuring pupils gain the knowledge, skills and confidence they need for GCSE, Sixth Form and beyond.
Underpinning our approach are the Claires Court Essentials, which encourage pupils to become resilient, resourceful and reflective learners. Rather than simply recalling information, girls are encouraged to think deeply, make connections across subjects and apply their learning in new situations.
Learning With Purpose
We believe the most effective learning happens when pupils are actively engaged in the process.
Across many subjects, learning is centred around carefully constructed questions and real-world challenges that encourage pupils to investigate, evaluate evidence and develop their own understanding. This problem-solving approach helps girls become confident, independent learners who are prepared for the demands of further study and future careers.
Our focus is on mastery, enabling pupils to develop secure, long-term understanding before moving on. By deepening knowledge rather than accelerating through content, girls gain the confidence to apply their learning creatively and independently.
Measuring Progress, Supporting Achievement
Regular feedback plays an important role in helping every pupil succeed.
Throughout the year, girls complete a programme of ongoing assessments and Common Tasks, with every pupil in the year group completing the same assessment in each subject once per term. This provides meaningful feedback for pupils, teachers and parents, helping to celebrate success while identifying areas for further development.
Parents and guardians receive regular updates through grade cards during the year, alongside detailed subject reports that provide a clear picture of academic progress and next steps.
Across the school, the academic curriculum provides a broad and coherent education for pupils of all ages, and fully supports the learning principles and philosophy of the School, and the high level of pupils’ achievements.– ISI Inspection Report

As pupils progress into Key Stage 4, they benefit from expert guidance to help them choose GCSE subjects that reflect their interests, strengths and future ambitions.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pastoral Care | Senior Girls | Claires Court

Senior Girls Pastoral Care
Supporting every step
A happy, confident pupil is far more likely to thrive, both academically and personally. At Claires Court, pastoral care is at the heart of school life, ensuring every girl feels known, valued and supported throughout her Senior School journey.
We understand that the teenage years bring exciting opportunities as well as new challenges. Through strong relationships with teachers, form tutors and families, we create an environment where every pupil feels confident to ask for support, celebrate success and develop the resilience to overcome setbacks.
Knowing every pupil
Every girl belongs to a form group led by a dedicated Form Tutor, who is the first point of contact for both pupils and parents.
Meeting with pupils every day, Form Tutors build strong relationships based on trust, encouragement and understanding. They guide girls through their Personal, Social, Health, Citizenship and Careers programme while supporting their academic progress and personal development.
By taking the time to know each pupil as an individual, Form Tutors help ensure every girl feels supported, listened to and encouraged to achieve her potential.
Wellbeing and academic success
Outstanding pastoral care and academic achievement go hand in hand.
Girls are most successful when they feel confident, secure and able to be themselves. That is why our pastoral support is closely linked with every aspect of school life, helping pupils build resilience, develop positive relationships and approach challenges with confidence.
Our aim is not simply to help girls achieve excellent examination results, but to equip them with the character, self belief and emotional wellbeing that will support them throughout Sixth Form, higher education and their future careers.
Celebrating character
Academic achievement is only one measure of success.
The Claires Court Key Value Award recognises pupils who consistently demonstrate the qualities that strengthen our school community, including responsibility, respect, integrity and positive citizenship.
Pupils build their own record of achievement, validated by both staff and peers, with awards presented as they progress through the school:
The programme encourages every girl to contribute positively to school life while recognising the importance of kindness, leadership and service to others.
Platinum
Specialist wellbeing support
Supporting wellbeing means ensuring help is always available when it is needed.
Our School Nurses play an important role within the pastoral team, providing support for physical health, emotional wellbeing and mental health throughout the school day.
Working alongside safeguarding and academic staff, they are based within dedicated wellbeing centres and have access to specialist counselling and psychological services where appropriate. Their expertise helps ensure every pupil receives the care and guidance she needs to flourish.
Girls on Board
Friendships are an important part of school life and learning how to navigate them is a valuable life skill.
Claires Court is proud to be a founding member and regional training hub for the Girls on Board programme, which supports girls aged 8 to 18 in building healthy friendships and developing the confidence to manage the natural challenges that can arise during adolescence.
Working alongside our experienced pastoral team and School Nurses, the programme helps girls strengthen their resilience, emotional awareness and interpersonal skills in a positive and supportive environment.
Working in partnership with families
The strongest support comes when school and home work together.
Regular communication between parents, Form Tutors and teachers helps ensure every girl receives consistent guidance throughout her time at Claires Court. Parents’ evenings, school events and our active Parent Teacher Association provide valuable opportunities to stay connected and involved in school life.
By building strong relationships with families, we create a supportive community where every pupil can flourish with confidence.
Discover the Claires Court difference
The best way to experience the supportive atmosphere at Claires Court is to visit us.
Meet our dedicated staff, discover our pastoral approach and see how we help every girl feel known, valued and confident to achieve her potential.

Sport for every pupil
Sport is an important part of life at Claires Court. Whether competing at a high level, representing the school or enjoying being active with friends, every girl is encouraged to develop confidence, resilience and a lifelong appreciation of physical activity.
Our approach balances participation with performance, ensuring every pupil is challenged to achieve her personal best while enjoying the many physical, social and emotional benefits that sport brings. Expert coaching, excellent facilities and a wide range of sporting opportunities help girls develop skills that extend far beyond the playing field.

Physical Education is designed to help pupils become confident, capable and intelligent performers.
Throughout their Senior Girls journey, pupils develop technical skills, tactical understanding and an appreciation of healthy, active lifestyles. Lessons encourage teamwork, decision making and resilience while helping girls understand the importance of physical and mental wellbeing.

Our talented coaching staff provide opportunities for pupils at every level, creating an environment where effort, commitment and personal progress are valued alongside success in competition.

Our enthusiastic and dedicated PE staff and specialist coaches aim to maximise the potential of every pupil teaching them the meaning of teamwork, patience, fair play and resilience. All children are encouraged to participate throughout their school journey.
We are delighted that many of our sporting team coach to an International level and are sports people in their own rights.

Excellent facilities and specialist teaching enable every girl to enjoy a varied and rewarding sporting experience.
Alongside our on site facilities, pupils benefit from access to a range of specialist venues for training and competition, including rowing, sailing and outdoor activities. pageCache.pageTitle: Our History | Claires Court School Maidenhead
pageCache.text:
History
Our History
Claires Court has been part of the Maidenhead community since 1960. From its beginnings as a small school for 20 boys, it has grown into an independent school for pupils and students aged 2 to 18, while retaining the close relationships and individual attention on which it was founded.
Today, Claires Court continues to evolve with confidence, combining more than 65 years of local heritage with the stability, expertise and investment that come from being part of a wider charitable education group.
Founded in Maidenhead
Claires Court was established in 1960 by David and Josephine Wilding as a preparatory day school for boys.
The school grew quickly. By 1970, more than 180 pupils were enrolled, and during the following two decades its age range expanded to provide education from Reception through to age 16.
Ridgeway, originally used as a boarding house, became the home of the younger pupils (nursery and junior school) and remains an important part of the school today.
Senior Boys
Senior Boys has been central to the Claires Court story from the very beginning. The school was founded in 1960 as a boys’ day prep school with just 20 pupils and expanded rapidly through the following decades. As the school grew, the age range widened and the Senior Boys community became established at Ray Mill Road East, where it remains today.
Welcoming girls
A significant new chapter began in 1993, when Claires Court took responsibility for Maidenhead College for Girls and secured the future of its College Avenue site.
This development brought girls into the Claires Court community and was followed by the opening of a coeducational Sixth Form in 1994.
The school developed a distinctive structure, with boys and girls learning together during their younger years, separately within the Senior Schools and together again in Sixth Form. This became known as the Diamond Model.
From September 2026, the Junior School became fully coeducational, continuing the school’s tradition of adapting thoughtfully to meet the needs of pupils and families.
Rooted in the local community
Claires Court has grown across three established sites in Maidenhead, each with its own character and facilities.
Over the years, the school has built strong relationships with local families, organisations, charities and sports clubs. These connections provide pupils with opportunities in areas including rowing, rugby, sailing, tennis, hockey and community service.
Generations of families have chosen Claires Court, creating a strong sense of identity, belonging and continuity across the school.
A secure new chapter
In February 2026, Claires Court joined the Licensed Trade Charity through LTC Education Group (LTCEG), its education arm.
The move marked a carefully planned next chapter for the school, providing long term stability, wider educational expertise and the ability to invest responsibly in its future.
Claires Court retains its name, identity, ethos and place within Maidenhead. Its established strengths are now supported by the resources and experience of a charitable group with more than 230 years of heritage and HM The King as its Patron.
Building on strong foundations
Throughout its history, Claires Court has continued to develop while remaining focused on the needs of each pupil.
The school today is shaped by the same qualities that have supported its growth since 1960: strong relationships, individual attention, broad opportunity and the confidence to look ahead.
This combination of heritage and forward thinking ensures Claires Court is well placed to support current pupils and serve Maidenhead families for generations to come.

The people behind Claires Court
Leadership Team and Staff
The quality of a school is shaped by its people. At Claires Court, experienced teachers, pastoral leaders and support staff work together to know, stretch and support every pupil and student.
Our leadership structure brings together expertise from across Nursery, Juniors, Senior Girls, Senior Boys and Sixth Form. This creates a connected approach to education, wellbeing and school improvement, while ensuring that each part of the school has leadership focused on the needs of its pupils.
#CCLoyalty #CCRespect #CCIntegrity #CCResponsibility
Senior Leadership Team
Governors
Responsibility for the provision of education at the schools owned by the Licensed Trade Charity is vested in the Trustee Body who will direct the Licensed Trade Charity Chief Executive in the formulation of education policy.
The Licensed Trade Charity Chief Executive’s delegated task is to manage the policy efficiently, to maintain oversight of the Schools and to provide a variety of support services. The Licensed Trade Charity Chief Executive will carry out his management responsibilities in partnership with the Director of Education (Mainstream) and the Governing Body.
The Chairman of the Claires Court Governing Body is Mr Toby Brett.
If you would like further information about the trustees or governing body, or to contact Mr Toby Brett, please email Clare Clark, Clerk to the Trustees: Clare.Clark@ltcharity.org.uk
